key_insight: CLIFT shows that web agents can train and improve themselves using conformal self-verification, reducing reliance on expensive external judges. This enables both better training signals and scalable test-time reasoning for browser tasks.
problem_solved: Reinforcement learning for web agents suffers from weak supervision: binary task success is too sparse for learning, while using frontier-model judges at every step is too costly and may not be available at deployment.
method: Uses conformal self-verification, where the agent checks its own intermediate answers against natural-language evidence/criteria.
Turns sparse success signals into denser training feedback, improving credit assignment during RL.
Applies the same self-verification mechanism at test time to scale performance without depending on an external judge.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, CLIFT offers a practical way to train web agents with stronger supervision signals while keeping costs low. It also makes deployment more realistic by removing the need for always-on frontier-model evaluation.

paper_title: CLIFT: Conformal Self-Verification for Web Agent Training and Test-Time Scaling
paper_authors: Yifan Zhang, Yutong Dai, Viraj Prabhu, Zhiyuan Hu, Ran Xu
